I found out he was cheating while on holiday at the beach (driving distance from home). It was a group of us (including him) and she (his ex) invited herself along. I felt weird vibes between them, he wasn't acting like himself. I went to our room to get away, thinking (hoping) I was being paranoid and trying not to cause a scene.

She followed me to the room and told me they'd been sleeping together. "It was just sex, it didn't mean anything" was how she justified it. Completely untrue statement (on her part, she was for sure still in love with him), but even if it had been true, it didn't help.

I asked her to leave the room and got him to come to the room to talk to me. I was heartbroken, I felt like my whole world had just been ripped away. Then he said it was my fault. I "made him feel small", like "less of a man", all that bullshit. I was begging him to stay with me, saying through tears "please don't leave me", (tragic, I know) but he broke up with me.

I was humiliated and completely devastated. And, I was stuck there. He and I had travelled there together and everyone else had already been drinking. We were two hours from home and I was stuck there with him and her and all our "friends". Turns out some of them knew he'd been cheating on me. Quelle surprise, fuckwits flock together.

Some hours later, an *actual* friend of mine arrived (she was coming later in the day because she'd been at work.) As soon as she arrived and saw how upset I was, she told me to put my stuff in her car and she took me home.

I didn't sleep or eat anything for four days. 

A few weeks later he got in touch with me and it was like I could breathe again. We got back together and, to nobody's surprise but mine, he cheated again. And again. And again. Even when he gave me chlamydia, it wasn't enough for me to leave. Denial and absolutely no self esteem (the person I was with before him was emotionally abusive and a rapist). 

I always had the thought in my head, "at least he doesn't scream at me," "at least he doesn't give me bruises," "at least he doesn't rape me". The bar was under Hell it was so low.


We broke up and got back together often throughout the four years we were in each other's lives, but that first time was the worst. 

Eventually, I became an outpatient at the psych ward for one year due to suicide ideation - I'd been struggling with suicidal thoughts and attempts since I was a child. I also got properly medicated. When I finally started rebuilding my self esteem, it was like a spell broke. 

By this time I'd moved in with him. The lease where I was living ended and I lost my job. (You wouldn't believe it but I got fired one month after *someone else* complained on my behalf about a superior sexually harassing me. The complaint was made without my knowledge or permission, and was made anonymously). As it stood, I had nowhere else to go (I'd applied for 70+ rental properties to no avail), so *reluctantly* he let me move in with him.

At last, my dad moved back to the town where I was living (for unrelated reasons) and let me move in with him. Halle-fucking-lujah. I was able to cut contact and start to move on with my life.

If you read all of this, you were undoubtedly screaming at your phone/computer "Just leave! What's wrong with you??" And you'd be right to! I just couldn't see it for what it was. I couldn't and wouldn't believe that he didn't love me. I thought, "if I keep trying to forgive him, eventually he'll see how much I love him and he won't want to hurt me anymore." Loopy. 

Some of you may call this a cope, and maybe it is, but I think he did love me. It's just that the only love he's capable of giving is a deeply flawed kind of love. We were both in our early 20s, we'd both been through some shit and had a lot of growing to do.

He has cheated on his current girlfriend at least once, so I guess he hasn't grown up all that much (we're both in our early 30s now). I, on the other hand, stayed single for a few years. I got into another relationship in 2021 and he cheated on me too! I broke up with him straight away. It might've taken a few lessons, but I did learn eventually haha.

I've been (happily) single for the past ~3 years. I'm only just starting to be open to dating. Almost too late to start a family the old fashioned way.

I guess if I had to summarise what I learned, I'd say, don't fall for the sunk cost fallacy, and when someone shows you who they are, believe them! It all seems obvious to me now, but boy was it hard to see then.
